summary: postinstall downloads and executes a binary from a bare-IP HTTPS endpoint with TLS verification disabled
details: The postinstall lifecycle script fetches a platform tarball from a hardcoded bare-IPv4 endpoint (https://218.90.133.98:4443/onecode_tgz/onecode-<version>/onecode-linux-x64-<version>.tgz) rather than from the @onescience publisher's own domain. The fetch uses `https.get(url, { rejectUnauthorized: false },...)`, explicitly disabling TLS certificate verification, and no hash or signature of the fetched bytes is verified before use. The received tarball is extracted with `tar -xzf`, chmod 0755'd, and hardlinked into `bin/.onecode` so it runs when the `onecode` CLI is invoked. The download base is also overridable via the `ONECODE_TGZ_DOWNLOAD_BASE` environment variable, further weakening pinning. Because the source is a bare IP with disabled TLS validation and no integrity check, any on-path attacker between the installer and the endpoint can substitute arbitrary executable bytes that will be staged and executed on the installer's machine at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
